title: Can Painted Hardwood Floors Be Refinished Back to Natural Wood?
meta: Yes, painted hardwood floors can usually be sanded back to bare wood and refinished. Wills Flooring in Lynnwood covers the lead test, the grain and the price.
keywords: refinish painted hardwood floors, can you sand painted wood floors, remove paint from hardwood floors, painted floor back to natural wood, hardwood floor refinishing Lynnwood WA

blocks.lead: Yes. A painted hardwood floor can almost always be sanded back to bare wood and refinished, as long as the boards are still thick enough and the paint is not hiding rot, plywood patches or lead you cannot disturb.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring sands painted floors at the same published rates as any other refinish: $3.99 per sq ft natural, $6.50 with stain, 500 sq ft minimum. The two questions we answer before quoting are whether the paint contains lead and what the paint was covering.

blocks.html: We see this question most in Lynnwood's 1960s and 70s ramblers and split-levels around Alderwood, Meadowdale and Martha Lake. Somebody painted the bedroom floors gray in the 90s, or a landlord rolled porch paint over the hallway between tenants, and the new owner pulls up a corner of carpet and finds oak under a coat of eggshell. The good news is that paint sits on the finish, not in the wood. Here is what actually happens when we sand it, what paint tends to hide, and the one situation where we tell you not to do it.

blocks.text: What happens when we sand a painted floor

items.d: Before the quote: test and probe
items.text: We swab the paint for lead, pull a floor vent or closet board to measure wood thickness, and scrape a test patch to see how many layers are on the floor and what species is underneath.
items.note: Most Lynnwood floors under paint are 3/4 in red oak; some are fir

items.text: Paint gums up sandpaper fast, so the first pass runs a coarser grit than a normal refinish and burns through two or three times the paper. On a thick paint job this pass alone can take most of a day.
items.note: Extra abrasives and time are quoted at the estimate

items.text: Edgers get the paint off along walls and under toe-kicks. Paint that ran into the gaps between boards is scraped by hand, because a sander cannot reach it.
items.note: This is where paint ghosting comes from if it is skipped

items.d: Day 2 to 3: finish sanding and coats
items.text: Once the wood is clean we sand exactly as we would any floor, then apply three coats of Bona water-based finish, or a stain plus finish if you chose color.

blocks.text: What the paint is usually hiding

items.title: Water stains and pet stains
items.text: Paint is the classic fix for a floor a previous owner could not clean. Dark rings and black urine spots under paint often sand out, but deep ones do not. We flag these at the test patch so a stain color can be chosen to hide them, or boards can be replaced.

items.title: Patches and plywood infill
items.text: Where a wall was moved or a heater removed, someone may have filled the hole with plywood or mismatched boards and painted over it. Refinishing exposes this. We can weave in matching oak, which is quoted per board on site.

items.title: Multiple layers and old varnish
items.text: Three coats of latex over shellac over a 1960s varnish is normal in Meadowdale. Each layer clogs paper differently. This is why a painted-floor quote is never a phone quote.

items.title: Fir instead of oak
items.text: Some Lynnwood homes have softer fir under paint. Fir refinishes at the same price but holds pigment in its soft grain, so a natural finish with satin sheen usually looks better than a stain.

blocks.text: Price your Lynnwood floor right now

blocks.note: Heavy paint removal and any board replacement are quoted on site after the test patch. Everything else in the calculator is our published rate.

blocks.text: Natural or stain after paint comes off

a.title: Go natural when
items: The test patch shows clean oak with no ghosting in the gaps
The house is a 1960s to 70s rambler and you want the original look
You want the cheapest full refinish and the fastest schedule
The floor is fir, which blotches under stain

b.title: Choose stain when
items: Traces of pigment remain in the open grain of oak
Old water marks sanded lighter but not away
You are matching new boards woven into the old floor
You want a color that fits the rest of the remodel

blocks.text: The lead question in Lynnwood homes

blocks.html: Almost every painted floor we see in Lynnwood is in a house built before 1978, which is the year lead was banned from residential paint. Floor paint from the 50s, 60s and early 70s can contain it. Sanding lead paint without containment spreads fine lead dust through the house, and that is a real health issue for children and pets, not a formality. We test the paint before we write a quote. If it comes back negative, the job proceeds like any refinish. If it comes back positive, the work needs lead-safe practices, full containment and cleanup, and the scope changes. We will tell you exactly what that means for price and schedule before you decide.

blocks.title: Do not DIY-sand a painted floor in a pre-1978 house:
blocks.text: Rental sanders have no real dust capture. A $12 lead swab from any hardware store tells you in five minutes whether the paint is safe to sand. Test first, then decide.
When you should not sand a painted floor

items.html: The wood is already thin. Some floors were painted after their last possible sanding. If less than 3/32 in remains above the tongue, another full sanding will expose nails and tongues. We measure before quoting.
Paint was hiding structural rot. Soft boards near an exterior door or under a bathroom threshold are a replacement job, not a refinish.
The floor is a mix of species and patches. A natural finish makes every patch visible. Stain helps, but a heavily pieced floor may look better replaced or covered.
You wanted a recoat. Our $1.99 screen-and-recoat only works over intact clear finish. Paint is not a finish it can bond to, so a painted floor always needs full sanding.

The paint is lead-positive and the budget is fixed. Lead-safe sanding costs more. If the extra puts the job out of reach, a sound painted floor can be repainted or covered instead, and the oak stays there for a future owner. See our guide to refinish or replace for the full decision.

blocks.text: How to get a clean result on a painted floor

items: Test the paint for lead yourself before the estimate, or let us do it at the visit. It changes everything about the scope.
Pull a corner of carpet or a closet board so we can see the wood and measure thickness on the first visit.
Ask for a scraped test patch in a hallway, not a closet. Hallways show wear and stains that closets hide.
Decide on stain versus natural after the test patch, not before. What is under the paint decides it.
Add dust containment ($250) if anyone lives in the house during the work. Paint dust is finer than wood dust.

faq.q: Does refinishing a painted hardwood floor cost more?
faq.a: The finish work is our published rate: $3.99 per sq ft natural or $6.50 with stain, 500 sq ft minimum. Heavy paint adds sanding time and abrasives, and lead-positive paint adds containment, so those are quoted on site after we scrape a test patch and swab the paint.

faq.q: Will all the paint come out of the grain?
faq.a: On red oak, almost always. Oak has open grain, but sanding to bare wood removes the paint with it. Where paint ran into gaps between boards it has to be hand-scraped. Fir is softer and can hold a trace of pigment, which is why we recommend a natural finish on fir.

faq.q: Can I just screen and recoat over floor paint?
faq.a: No. A screen-and-recoat at $1.99 per sq ft only works over an intact clear finish that new finish can bond to. Paint is not that. A painted floor needs full sanding to bare wood, then three coats of finish.

faq.q: How do I know if the paint has lead?
faq.a: Any hardware store sells lead swabs for about $12. Rub one on a scraped edge and it turns red if lead is present. In Lynnwood homes built before 1978 we assume it might be and test before quoting. A positive result means lead-safe practices and full containment.

faq.q: Can a painted floor be stained a dark color instead of natural?
faq.a: Yes, and stain is often the better choice on a painted floor because it hides faint ghosting and old water marks that sanded lighter but not away. Sand, stain and finish is $6.50 per sq ft. We test the color on your floor before committing.

faq.q: How long does a painted floor refinish take?
faq.a: Add about a day to a normal refinish. A 700 to 900 sq ft Lynnwood main floor usually runs three to four days for natural finish, four to five with stain, including dry time between coats.
